title: Le Peuple de la mer
summary: "Le Peuple de la mer" by Marc Elder is a novel published in 1913. This Prix Goncourt-winning work presents three interconnected chronicles set in the village of L'Herbaudière on the island of Noirmoutier. The novel portrays the interwoven destinies of sailors, fishermen, and lighthouse keepers who make their lives along the Atlantic coast. Through these chronicles—titled The Boat, the Woman, and the Sea—Elder captures the rhythms and struggles of a maritime community bound to the ocean's unforgiving embrace.
